subject: paediatrics
title: Chromosomal disorders in children: Down Turner Klinefelter

steps.tx: **Down syndrome** is recognised by hypotonia, upslanting palpebral fissures, Brushfield spots, a single palmar crease and a sandal gap. **Turner syndrome** affects short girls with webbed neck, shield chest and widely spaced nipples, while Klinefelter syndrome affects tall boys with gynaecomastia and small firm testes. Screening uses nuchal thickness and cell free DNA testing, while amniocentesis with karyotype confirms the diagnosis. Counselling explains age related risk and recurrence for the family.
steps.say: Down syndrome causes hypotonia with distinctive facial features. Turner syndrome affects short girls with a webbed neck. Klinefelter syndrome affects tall boys with small testes. Karyotype confirms the diagnosis after screening tests.

steps.tx: Children with Down syndrome associate with **AV canal**, ventricular septal defect, duodenal atresia with a double bubble, Hirschsprung disease, leukaemia and hypothyroidism. Turner syndrome associates with **coarctation**, horseshoe kidney, streak gonads and thyroid disease, while Klinefelter syndrome associates with infertility, language delay and metabolic problems. Growth is short in Down and Turner syndromes but tall in Klinefelter syndrome. Newborn cardiac echocardiography and Turner renal ultrasound hunt these associations early.
steps.say: Down syndrome associates with cardiac and bowel anomalies. Turner syndrome associates with coarctation and horseshoe kidney. Klinefelter syndrome associates with infertility and language delay. Early echocardiography and ultrasound hunt these associated problems.

steps.tx: This four chamber echocardiogram shows a **common AV valve** guarding both ventricles instead of separate mitral and tricuspid valves. Below it, the atrial septum lacks its lower part, which is the **primum defect** of an AV canal. The right and left atria and ventricles are labelled around the defect. This anatomy matters because AV canal is the classic cardiac lesion of Down syndrome and newborn echocardiography must look for it.
steps.say: This echocardiogram shows a common valve guarding both ventricles. The lower atrial septum is absent in a primum defect. Together these features form an atrioventricular canal defect. The lesion associates strongly with Down syndrome in children.

vis.alt: Four chamber echocardiogram showing common atrioventricular valve and primum septal defect labeled.
vis.caption: Echocardiogram showing common AV valve and primum defect. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Management begins with early echocardiography so cardiac repair is planned in time. **Thyroid function** is checked yearly in Down syndrome and thyroxine replaces deficiency when found. Turner syndrome may need growth hormone trials and oestrogen to induce puberty, while **Klinefelter syndrome** may need testosterone. Early intervention with physiotherapy and speech therapy supports development, eye and hearing screening detects treatable problems, and genetics teams discuss recurrence while schools support learning.
steps.say: Early echocardiography plans cardiac repair at the right time. Thyroid function needs yearly checks in Down syndrome. Hormones are inducing puberty in Turner and Klinefelter syndromes. Early therapy supports development, speech and learning together.

steps.tx: Important traps close this lesson for safe practice. A missed duct dependent **cardiac lesion** can collapse a newborn, and **atlantoaxial instability** warns against forceful neck manipulation in Down syndrome. Turner syndrome risks aortic dissection with hypertension, Y material in gonads risks tumour, and Klinefelter syndrome rarely links with breast cancer. Bruising or pallor needs leukaemia vigilance, translocation carriers in the family need testing, and adult transition with respectful disclosure completes care.
steps.say: Missed cardiac lesions can suddenly collapse a newborn during the first days of life. Neck manipulation needs caution in Down syndrome. Turner syndrome is risking aortic dissection with hypertension. Family carriers of translocations need genetic testing offered promptly for future pregnancy planning.
